findings.title: consoleChange exported from scene.ts breaks the two test files that vi.mock the scene module
findings.claim: Task 5 puts `consoleChange` in `app/duel/scene.ts`. Both `duelMode.ts` and `onlineDuel.ts` are told to call it when they are created. Two existing tests replace that module with a vi.mock factory that returns only `createDuelScene`. In Vitest, reading an export the factory did not define throws ("No 'consoleChange' export is defined on the mock"). So `startDuelMode` throws in duelModeDispose.test.ts, and `createOnlineDuelSession` throws in every test in onlineDuelSession.test.ts.
findings.evidence: plan L983-989 (export consoleChange from scene.ts), L1025 (onlineDuel: `const trackConsole = consoleChange(...)` right after the keyboard), L1033 (duelMode: same, at creation), L1041 (Step 4 expects tests/duelModeDispose.test.ts and tests/onlineDuelSession.test.ts to PASS); tests/duelModeDispose.test.ts:L12-17 (scene mock has only createDuelScene); tests/onlineDuelSession.test.ts:L60-72 (scene mock has only createDuelScene); src/renderer/src/app/duel/duelMode.ts:L34-36 and onlineDuel.ts:L67-69 (where the call would go, run at creation).
findings.why: Task 5 Step 4 fails as written: one test in duelModeDispose and the whole onlineDuelSession suite. The subagent has no instruction for this, and the plan says no existing test changes unless a task names it.
findings.fix: Put `consoleChange` in a small module of its own that no test mocks, for example `src/renderer/src/app/duel/consoleChange.ts`, which imports only `type ConsoleStation`. Import it from there in duelMode.ts and onlineDuel.ts, and export it there for the test. Or add `consoleChange: () => () => {}` to both mock factories and name those two test edits in Task 5.

findings.title: Readout rows, help and map reserves follow the view, not whether the console is drawn
findings.claim: The scene passes `console: true` to `readoutRows`, gives empty help and uses `CONSOLE_RESERVE` whenever `view !== 'interior'`. The console view is null while paused, on the end card and under any banner, and then DuelUi puts the readout back in the right-hand column. So on a paused Weapons screen the right column loses LOCK, CHARGE and MAG (the station block that shows them is hidden) and loses its key help. Off-screen arrows are then only kept 156 px from the right edge, so they can pass under the 220 px readout column.
findings.evidence: plan L1010 (`console: true ... when view !== 'interior'`, `help: view === 'interior' ? readoutHelp(view) : []`, the reserves always 228/156); plan L908-909 (placement is 'status' only when `duel.console && station !== 'ship'`); plan L23 (the console view is null while paused or under a banner); readoutModel.ts:L76-83 (the LASER, LOCK, CHARGE and MAG rows the console flag removes); readoutModel.ts:L103-106 (help).
findings.why: Escape (pause) is ordinary play. The pause screen would show a readout with no laser information and no key help, and arrows could overlap the readout. That is not today's paused screen, and the plan does not state the change.
findings.fix: In `draw`, compute `const hidden = consoleHidden(d, overlay, source.paused())` before the tactical input. Use `onConsole = !hidden && view !== 'interior'` to choose the reserves (`CONSOLE_RESERVE` or `reserveRight: READOUT_COLUMN`), the `console` flag on `readoutRows` and the help (`onConsole ? [] : readoutHelp(view)`). Add a sceneUi or scene test for a paused Weapons frame.

findings.title: Moving INTERIOR_BAND to y 42 breaks worldFit.test.ts, which Task 2 neither lists nor runs; the duelInterior line numbers are wrong
findings.claim: With the band at y 42 and h 678, the Cutter's fit y becomes 42 + (678 − 416) / 2 = 173, not 152. worldFit.test.ts:L56 hard-codes `{ scale: 1, x: 66, y: 152 }`, and it is missing from Task 2's run list and its git add. In duelInterior.test.ts the hard-coded 152 is at L41-42, L89, L92 and L102, but the plan names L43-44 (lines that do not change).
findings.evidence: plan L454 (band change; list of tests to run), L527 (Step 4 run list, no worldFit), L535 (git add, no worldFit), L262 (`update tests/duelInterior.test.ts:43-44 only if its assertions change`); tests/worldFit.test.ts:L56; tests/duelInterior.test.ts:L41-42, L89, L102; tests/interiorCamera.test.ts:L9, L29; src/renderer/src/render/duel/interiorModel.ts:L13.
findings.why: The Task 2 subagent will not see the failure. It then appears in Task 5 Step 5's full suite, in a task with no instruction to fix it, which breaks the 'tests pass unchanged except where a task names them' rule.
findings.fix: In Task 2, name tests/worldFit.test.ts:L56, tests/duelInterior.test.ts:L41-42/L89/L102 and tests/interiorCamera.test.ts:L9/L29. Give the new value (y 173 at stage 1, or derived from INTERIOR_BAND). Add worldFit.test.ts to the Step 4 run list and to the git add.

findings.title: The 'console and repair both in reach' tab test can pass without exercising the rule
findings.claim: The case puts player 0 on the first repair point in the Weapons console's room and expects `tabs.weapons === 'locked'`. If that tile is not in reach of the console, `consoleInReach` returns −1 and the tab is locked anyway, so the test passes without testing the `repairInReach < 0` condition. The plan itself is unsure such a point exists on the cutter. The cutter's Weapons repair point is (8,7), and duelControls reaches the console from (9,6).
findings.evidence: plan L361-371 (the case and its hedge); src/renderer/src/sim/duel/tuning.ts:L13 (cutter W repair point [8,7]); tests/duelControls.test.ts:L68-69 ((9,6) is beside the Weapons console); src/renderer/src/app/duel/controls.ts:L21-41 (both helpers).
findings.why: This is the one rule that separates sitting from repairing (spec §6.3, §8 'including a standing player next to an empty console with a repair in reach'). A vacuous pass leaves it untested.
findings.fix: Before the expectation, assert `consoleInReach(d, 0) === d.weapons` and `repairInReach(d, 0) >= 0`. If no tile on the cutter or the Hound satisfies both, test the rule by stubbing the two inputs (for example, factor the tab rule into a pure function of seat, console in reach and repair in reach).

findings.title: consoleHidden does not hide the console online in phases other than running and paused
findings.claim: Spec §6.1 says the console is null online in any phase other than `running`. The plan's `consoleHidden` uses `source.paused()` (online: phase === 'paused') and banner !== null. So the publication phases 'ended' and 'error' still draw a clickable console, although pump() drops all input outside 'running'. The deviation is not stated.
findings.evidence: spec L234-236; plan L1005-1007; src/renderer/src/app/duel/onlineSource.ts:L135 (paused = phase 'paused'); src/renderer/src/net/contracts.ts:L116 (phases running, paused, ended, error); onlineDuel.ts:L200 (input dropped unless running).
findings.why: In those phases the buttons look clickable but do nothing.
findings.fix: Add a `running()` to DuelViewSource (runtime: `!paused() && !ended()`; online: `publication()?.phase === 'running'`) and use it in `consoleHidden`. Or list this under the plan's deviations.

findings.title: Task 5 names the wrong runtime interface location; two of its test snippets are sketches
findings.claim: Task 5 points at 'the DuelRuntime interface near L40-50' and 'the one that lists `axes(): Axes;`'. L40-60 is FlightRuntime, and FlightRuntime also lists `axes(): Axes;`; DuelRuntime is at L167-207. The consoleHidden test refers to 'a running duel d (as the file's other tests build one)', but sceneUi.test.ts builds no duel and the snippet lists no imports (createDuel, layout, Outcome, consoleHidden). The Task 6 probe test also leaves out its `duelProbeFixture` import.
findings.evidence: plan L937, L1014; src/renderer/src/app/duel/runtime.ts:L42-60 (FlightRuntime, `axes(): Axes;` at L47) and L167-207 (DuelRuntime, L188); plan L955-964; tests/sceneUi.test.ts:L1-6 (no duel); plan L1069-1073; tests/uiProbe.test.ts imports (no duelProbeFixture).
findings.why: A subagent following the line hint could add `mode` and `uiHeld` to FlightRuntime and break createFlightRuntime. tsc would catch it, but only after the fact.
findings.fix: Point at `DuelRuntime` (runtime.ts:L167-207). Write the consoleHidden test out in full, with its imports and the duel fixture (parseShip(cutter), createDuel). Add the uiProbe import.

findings.title: Task 6's F10 step does nothing in the production build, and the CRT 'off' setting would not show the off-CRT button look anyway
findings.claim: Step 6 builds with `npx electron-vite build`, but F10 cycles the CRT setting only when `import.meta.env.DEV` is true. Also, the setting only changes the strength of the CRT effects. The off-CRT button palette (DIM/TEXT/AMBER) appears only when `crt` is false, which `crtActive(view)` gives only on the interior view.
findings.evidence: plan L1084, L1090; src/renderer/src/app/crtBoot.ts:L12; src/renderer/src/main.ts:L58 (`dev: import.meta.env.DEV`); src/renderer/src/app/duel/scene.ts:L105 (`crt: crtActive(view)`); plan L20 (the off-CRT button states).
findings.why: The look check will not produce the weapons-off screenshot as written, and it never checks the off-CRT button colours.
findings.fix: Seed the CRT localStorage key before launch (or use a dev build) for the 'off' strength. Check the off-CRT palette on the SHIP tab (interior) screenshot, where the tab strip draws with `crt` false.
